presentation.label: EUCLIDEAN TRIGS
presentation.summary: Analog Rytm-style Euclidean sequencer: two pulse generators, rotations and a logic operator write real trigs on an audio track.
presentation.overview: Euclid Seq adds an EUCLID trig mode and turns an audio track's trigs into a Euclidean rhythm, as the Analog Rytm's Euclidean mode does. Two generators (PL1, PL2) spread their pulses evenly over the track's length; RO1 and RO2 rotate each, OP combines them (OR, XOR, AND, SUB) and TRO rotates the result. The module writes ordinary trigs into the pattern, so the stock sequencer plays them with its own tempo, track speed, swing, locks and conditions; it keeps no clock. While EUC is on, the TRIG keys cannot add or remove trigs on that track; holding a trig still edits its parameter locks. The track's LFOs can modulate every setting from LFO SETUP's PMTR list; a modulated track plays the generator's pulses live while its stored trigs stay as set.
highlights: PL1/PL2 pulses, RO1/RO2/TRO rotations and OR/XOR/AND/SUB, per track and pattern
Writes real trigs: stock playback, swing, locks, conditions and bank save
LFO destinations: any track LFO can modulate PL1, PL2, RO1, RO2, TRO or OP; the rhythm moves live
An EUCLID trig mode with its own main-screen panel; FUNC+RIGHT opens the six-dial EUCLID page
Follows PATTERN SCALE length changes; no clock of its own
usage: Hold FUNC and press DOWN until TRIG MODE shows EUCLID (audio tracks). The main screen shows the EUCLID panel.
Press FUNC+RIGHT to open the EUCLID page and YES to turn EUC on. A sets PL1, B PL2, D RO1, E RO2, F TRO and LEVEL the operator; C shows the track length.
Press NO to close the page. The page also opens with RIGHT on TRACK TRIG EDIT's TRIGS row. Press YES on the page again to turn EUC off; the trigs remain as ordinary trigs.
For modulation, open LFO SETUP (FUNC+LFO) and turn PMTR past FX2 to EUC PL1, PL2, RO1, RO2, TRO or OP; DEP sets how far the LFO moves it.

limitations: Deliberate stock-flow changes: TRIG MODE gets a seventh row, EUCLID, on audio tracks; in that mode FUNC+RIGHT opens the EUCLID page instead of shifting trigs in grid recording; RIGHT on TRACK TRIG EDIT's TRIGS row opens the page; with EUC on, the TRIG keys, live recording and the FUNC+LEFT/RIGHT trig shift do not place, remove or move trigs on that track; on MKII in grid recording the trig keys show those trigs purple; the project file gets #EUCLID_SEQ= lines (comments the stock loader skips).

EUC settings are saved with the project (#EUCLID_SEQ= lines) and kept over a power cycle in battery RAM 0x100f9000..0x100fd010. They belong to their bank, pattern and track: track, pattern and TRACK TRIG EDIT TRIGS-row copy, paste, clear and undo carry or reset them. The EUCLID trig mode is runtime state like the stock trig mode and starts as TRACKS after a reboot.

LFO destinations: LFO SETUP's PMTR continues past FX2 into six EUCLID destinations; the Part stores the LFO's own speed as a stock-safe placeholder and the module keeps the destination in battery RAM 0x100fd100..0x100fd710 (saved Part copies 0x100fd800..0x100fde10) and #EUCLID_LFO= / #EUCLID_LFS= project lines. Track copy and paste, Part copy, paste, clear, undo, SAVE PART and RELOAD PART carry them; a project saved before the saved table existed loads with saved destinations equal to the working ones.

A modulated EUC track's pulses are decided per step; added pulses play without locks (unless on a trigless lock trig) and firmware look-ahead (sample preload, slide searches) reads the stored pattern, not the live pulses.
Purple trigs need the MKII panel; MKI trig LEDs stay stock.
Audio tracks only; MIDI tracks are not supported.

Functional MKII reports for the page, purple trigs, blocking, the EUCLID trig mode (VACEUCLID2, VACEUCLID4), saving with the project and a power cycle (VACEUCLID5), and a short summary of card saves, copies and a power cycle (VACEUCLID8); LFO modulation, Part reload, undo and the MKI are emulator-tested only; worst-case chip timing is unmeasured.
Like every DRAM module, the build gives up about 10 MB of sample memory to the platform reserve.

processing.label: ColdFire processing
processing.display: ≤ 2,304 instructions per audio frame (24 routed LFOs)
processing.conditions: ot_emu instruction counts on VACEUCLID8 with all 24 LFOs on EUCLID destinations; equal to the static longest path. The sequencer step path adds up to 5,775 instructions a step for eight modulated tracks. Chip cycles not measured. See TESTING.md, Performance.

impact.conditions: Eight EUC tracks with all 24 LFOs on EUCLID destinations, playing in grid recording; knob turns on the EUCLID page regenerate one track.

cpu.rationale: Every frame each LFO passes a short check (about 20 instructions, 96 when routed to a EUCLID destination); each step adds up to a few hundred instructions per modulated EUC track. Knob, copy and project events run on the UI task.

dsp.rationale: No DSP code, tables or buffers; stock DSP processing is unchanged.

memory.rationale: About 19 KB of code and state in the shared platform reserve and 19.5 KB of free battery RAM for the settings and LFO tables; no per-instance copies.

tests.summary: Host gates: the generator matches an independent formulation on 633,984 settings; LFO modulation on 40,000 settings; project-file lines (settings, LFO destinations, saved Part copies) round-trip and malformed lines are ignored. Emulator on the VACEUCLID8 image and a byte-identical build of the merged source: 34/34 scripted checks on the MKII and the MKI panel, 54/54 copy, paste, clear, undo, Part save and reload checks on both panels, 15/15 saving checks on both, plus LFO destinations, live pulses, slide look-ahead and stock-safety checks. Functional MKII reports on VACEUCLID2, VACEUCLID4, VACEUCLID5 and VACEUCLID8 (card saves, a power cycle with copied tracks, patterns and Parts, playback and display). No stress run, no chip timing.

conditions.parameterExtremes: Every LFO on a EUCLID destination takes the module's routed path, the dearest one (96 executed instructions, equal to its static longest path); settings PL1 5-10, PL2 3, RO1 2 on all eight tracks, EUC on.
conditions.parameterModulation: All 24 LFOs (3 per audio track) on EUCLID destinations PL1, RO1 and TRO with DEP raised, playing; LFOs on stock destinations take the cheaper unrouted path. Scenes and parameter locks do not reach this path.
conditions.modeSwitching: Grid recording on while playing (the LED painter's live-pulse path also runs); EUCLID trig mode and page open and closed during setup. Part changes were exercised in the copy suite, not under this measurement.
conditions.maxLoad: Eight audio tracks x three LFOs = 24 routed calls in every frame, measured over 8,276 frames (3 s). Cycles = executed instructions x 32 (allowance; chip cycles unmeasured); budget one 362.8 us frame at 264 MHz. The sequencer's step path (up to 5,775 instructions a step, another context) is measured separately in TESTING.md.
conditions.inputConditions: No audio path: the module adds no DSP code and reads no audio. MIDI tracks are not supported and take no module path.

memory.conditions: From the linked unit of the merged source build (m68k-elf-size -A out/platform/runtime/runtime.elf; .bss 0, every piece of state is explicitly initialised) and the module's battery-RAM layout; one table for every bank, pattern, Part and track, no per-track copies; no heap, DSP memory or cave space. The shared octabam loader and the platform's 10 MB DRAM reserve are not the module's own.

hardware.summary: On an Octatrack MKII the author loaded VACEUCLID8 and reported that three checks “seem correct”: project saves to the card including SAVE AS NEW (no save reported hanging); a copied Euclid track, a copied pattern and a copied Part with an EUC LFO destination came back after a save and a power cycle; pasted tracks played in time, the trig keys showed purple and the EUCLID page showed the pasted settings. Earlier images: page, purple trigs, blocking and the EUCLID trig mode (VACEUCLID2, VACEUCLID4), saving with the project and a power cycle (VACEUCLID5).
limitations: A short summary report, not step-by-step results or a timed stress run; no audio or timing measurement.
One MKII; no MKI (MKI behaviour is emulator-only).
LFO modulation and live pulses were not separately reported on hardware beyond the VACEUCLID8 summary.
Number of saves, the exact copies made, Part reload, undo and cross-bank pattern copies were not reported.
No combination with other modules on the unit for this image; the emulator-only card-write stall in TESTING.md was not seen, which does not show it cannot occur.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: Select track 1 with a sample. Hold FUNC and press DOWN until TRIG MODE shows EUCLID, then release FUNC.
Press FUNC+RIGHT to open EUCLID, then press YES: EUC ON writes four trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13.
Turn A to PL1 5 and B to PL2 3, then turn LEVEL to XOR: steps where only one generator pulses keep a trig. Press PLAY to hear it.
Turn F to rotate the whole rhythm, then press NO: the EUCLID panel shows 5:3, XOR and the new trigs.

Hold FUNC and press LFO for LFO SETUP. With LFO 1 selected, turn A (PMTR) all the way right, then back until it shows EUC PL1; turn F (DEP) up and press NO. Press PLAY: the pulse count rises and falls with the LFO, and the trig LEDs follow it in grid recording. Turn DEP to 0 or YES on the EUCLID page (EUC off) to stop it.

access.location: Audio track: FUNC+UP/DOWN (TRIG MODE) chooses EUCLID; FUNC+RIGHT then opens the EUCLID page. Also RIGHT on TRACK TRIG EDIT's TRIGS row.
steps: Include Euclid Seq in your build and select an audio track.
Hold FUNC and press DOWN until TRIG MODE shows EUCLID; release FUNC.
Press FUNC+RIGHT to open the EUCLID page; press YES to turn EUC on.
Press NO to close the page. In grid recording, FUNC+BANK then RIGHT on the TRIGS row opens it too.
